label: Reported held-out test results (Phase 3 / Phase 4)

provenance.note: These values are transcribed verbatim from the project's own progress presentation. Phase 3 and Phase 4 metric files were not present in results/metrics/, and the trained classical model artifacts (logistic_regression.joblib, random_forest.joblib, xgboost.joblib) were not present in models/, so these numbers cannot be recomputed by the application. Nothing here is derived, rounded, rescaled or inferred.

phase3.title: Phase 3 — Classical ML comparison
notes: XGBoost provided the strongest held-out classification metrics among the three classical models.
Repeated stratified 5-fold CV × 5: XGBoost Macro F1 = 0.880 ± 0.054; High F1 = 0.778 ± 0.148.
XGBoost was retained as the classical baseline for comparison with the MLP.

phase4.title: Phase 4 — MLP loss comparison
notes: Selected weighted MLP repeated CV: Macro F1 = 0.877 ± 0.077; High F1 = 0.778 ± 0.206.
Gradient-flow verification on real standardized test samples: finite and non-zero High-class gradients.
Weighted CE selected as the final differentiable MLP for counterfactual optimization.

comparison_note: XGBoost performs strongly among the classical models, while the weighted MLP achieved the highest reported held-out Macro F1 among the evaluated models. The MLP is used for Phase 5 because its differentiability enables gradient-based counterfactual optimization. Only 6 High-risk records exist in the held-out test set, so High-class metrics carry wide uncertainty and no single model should be described as universally best.
